mbm-2851.clue: The count-in comes from the window.
mbm-2851.quote: Our rehearsal room faces a pedestrian crossing. We start the first tune when the little green man appears. Once a group waiting to cross took our drum count for their signal and danced across together.

mbm-2852.clue: My chair has one sailor's knot.
mbm-2852.quote: The canvas on our deck chair split, so I lashed one corner with the knot my uncle taught me. In the sunshine it looks like a tiny fishing boat. I can sail through a whole afternoon without standing up.

mbm-2853.clue: I keep a small sea in my pocket.
mbm-2853.quote: After my first ocean swim I found a blue glass bead in the sand. I carry it to indoor practice. When the water smells like chlorine I roll it between my fingers and think of waves.

mbm-2854.clue: The banker wears my sister's bracelet.
mbm-2854.quote: When my sister turned banker at board-game night, she wore a bracelet with a tiny bell so we could hear the till open. The bracelet lives in the game box now. A silent loan doesn't count.

mbm-2855.clue: My green diamond has a secret hem.
mbm-2855.quote: My daughter's first dress had broad seams Dad could let out as she grew. I pieced the final green scrap into a quilt and left the seam folded. It still has a little growing room.

mbm-2856.clue: I paint the cloud that gets away.
mbm-2856.quote: I draw the shape of one cloud on a postcard and try to fill it before the wind changes it. My best picture is a cloud that began as a horse and ended as a very surprised chicken.

mbm-2857.clue: You can hear the mud breathe.
mbm-2857.quote: When the tide turns in our estuary I float my kayak still and listen to bubbles popping on the flats. My nephew heard it on tape and asked why my boat was cooking pancakes.

mbm-2858.clue: Our campsite had a doorbell for three days.
mbm-2858.quote: A cowbell without a clapper turned up in the campsite's lost box. We hung it by our tent and gave visitors a spoon to ring it with. The camp host joined us for cards every night just so he could make an entrance.

mbm-2859.clue: My first baduk board was a biscuit lid.
mbm-2859.quote: My grandfather ruled lines on the lid and taught me with black beans and white beans. I play on a wooden board now but keep three dry beans in its drawer for the teacher.

mbm-2860.clue: I gave the quilt a hole on purpose.
mbm-2860.quote: My sister wanted a quilted cover for the bread dough but kept lifting it to have a look. I stitched a little round viewing flap in the middle. Now the dough wears a patchwork hat and she can check how tall it's getting.

mbm-2861.clue: My cleanest victory had one thumb missing.
mbm-2861.quote: Our old arcade cabinet lost the cap on its action button. The owner lent me a big blue plastic coat button and covered the hole with it. I beat the level, then used my winnings to sew it back on his coat. He still calls it his lucky button.

mbm-2862.clue: My old belt holds our practice pads together.
mbm-2862.quote: I didn't know what to do with a belt I'd outgrown, so I tied the smallest training pads in a bundle with it. It still comes out on the mat before I do.

mbm-2863.clue: We played the song through the letterbox first.
mbm-2863.quote: I couldn't get our new brass section to come in softly enough. A neighbor stood outside the rehearsal room and opened the mail slot a little at a time. That tiny brass flap taught us our quietest entrance. The neighbor has an honorary spot in the band photo.

mbm-2864.clue: I cut my family's shortest queue.
mbm-2864.quote: At the noodle shop Mum served from one end and Dad cleared plates from the other. I folded a long strip of red paper into an accordion and cut out a row of diners passing bowls down the line. We hang it over the counter at closing time.

mbm-2865.clue: The bowling alley has a poem on the wall.
mbm-2865.quote: Someone pressed four old score pencils into the plaster over lane six like little lines of verse. After a good spare I look up there. The third pencil is the same deep red Gran used to score with.

mbm-2866.clue: I made a quilt for an empty chair.
mbm-2866.quote: Dad's old reading chair creaked at the same place every time he sat down. When he moved in with us, I quilted a cushion to fit the wooden seat. I left his favorite corner a little thinner. He settled back, heard the creak and asked who'd saved his place.

mbm-2867.clue: I learned the turn from our ceiling lamp.
mbm-2867.quote: When we practice ballroom at home the chain on the old lamp sways as we pass. If it keeps still on the next turn we're drifting toward the shelf. The lamp has saved the china three times.

mbm-2868.clue: I have a tent peg that smells of cinnamon.
mbm-2868.quote: I packed one wooden peg in the spice bag by mistake. All weekend the corner of our tent smelled like pastries. We kept that peg for the corner where the cook sleeps.

mbm-2869.clue: I keep an empty platform in a photo frame.
mbm-2869.quote: I took the station photo just after the last train left, with one trail of steam still hanging there. My little brother always asks where the engine went. I tell him the picture has just missed it too.

mbm-2870.clue: My map has a soup stain at the summit.
mbm-2870.quote: I spilled carrot soup while I was tracing our ridge walk and gave the summit an orange halo. We followed that map again in the snow. The bright orange summit had been warm and waiting all year.

mbm-2871.clue: I let one dragonfly play through.
mbm-2871.quote: I stood over a putt and a dragonfly settled on the end of my club. I waited till it lifted off, took the stroke and sank it. My partner marked a little blue wing beside the score.

mbm-2872.clue: I brought the longest note on our tour.
mbm-2872.quote: When my friend's bike bell broke, I whistled for both of us at the little blind bends. By the third village he had learned a harmony. We tried it in the tunnel on the way out and made ourselves laugh so hard we stopped for a minute.

mbm-2873.clue: I have the foggiest scorecard in the club.
mbm-2873.quote: On a foggy morning the first green vanished, so our foursome stayed in the clubhouse and drew the course from memory. The groundskeeper picked my card. He said I was the only one who remembered the drain where his keys fell in.

mbm-2874.clue: The newest chair gets the oldest blanket.
mbm-2874.quote: We watch our favorite TV comedy in pajamas at my sister's. She has a new armchair but covers it with our worn childhood blanket. The laugh track starts and we're sitting in the same room we grew up in.

mbm-2875.clue: I keep a postcard of a door in my notebook.
mbm-2875.quote: When a story stalls I draw the room behind that door. Last time it had a great barrel of lemons and one violin. My detective finally had somewhere interesting to go.
